sulphate reduction with H(2), but not with DOC, is the dominant sulphate reduction process in deep Fennoscandia and that the community is able to mitigate the increase in E (h) caused by repeated O (2) pulses as long as H (2) is available.

the sulphate-reductions of deep groundwater communities is dependent on the presence of H(2), and that the community is able to mitigate increases in E(h) induced by O(2) additions as long as H2 is present.

sulphate-reductions rates in a subterranean sulphate-reduing community were dependent on H(2) concentrations and that H(2)-dependent sulphate reduction may be an important process in deep Fennoscandia groundwater.

the sulphate-reducting microbial community was able to maintain a reducing environment in spite of the introduction of O(2).

the microbial activity in deep Fennoscandia is not only dependent upon the presence of H(2), but is also strongly influenced by the redox conditions.
